meta-description: A skill tree is a graph of the skills and concepts in one school subject, written by a teacher. Each node carries an instruction you copy into an AI chat.
hero-lede: A method for teaching and making teaching resources with AI. It is open, free, and needs no login.
hero-img-alt: A screen recording of the method in use: nodes in a skill tree are opened, their AI instructions copied, and the nodes ticked off as mastered.
what-p1: A tree lists the skills and concepts of a subject as nodes, with an arrow from each node to the ones it builds on. The whole subject is visible at once, so a student can choose where to start and see what a given skill depends on.
what-p2: The site does not call a language model. Each node composes a text instruction that you copy into whichever AI chat you already use, which means there is no account to create, no cost per student and no data processing agreement. The instructions are written to have the model ask questions rather than give answers.
tile-1-body: Browse the subjects that have a tree, and see what a finished tree and a single node look like.
tile-2-body: Make a tree with an AI chat, change it on screen and download it for your students.
tile-3-body: Send in a tree you have made, to have it published in the catalogue here under your name.
tile-4-body: The released version of the method, and how to cite it.
